New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to go up in about 7 days. App Total Revenue is -29.8% right now, so this points to a recovery rather than more weakness.

ios.head: Expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days — fewer of the people installing are subscribing.
ios.body: App Total New Subs is +30.7% while App Total Install is +84.2% — fewer of the people who installed are subscribing (-53.5pp less growth). New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to weaken in about 7 days. App Total Revenue is +14.0% right now, so expect that to cool off.

ios.head: App Total Install +84.2% — Organic Install is behind most of it (+2,112, +237.6%).
ios.body: App Total Install (YMK · US) was 5,979, against 3,245 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of +2,734. Where that came from: Organic Install +2,112 (+237.6%), Paid Install +623 (+28.6%), SEO Install +1 (+0.9%). Organic Install moved the most on its own (+2,112, +237.6%) and is now 50.2% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

ios.head: US is doing better than YMK overall on App Total Revenue (+14.0% vs +1.2%).
ios.body: App Total Revenue for US is +14.0%, while YMK overall is +1.2% — a gap of +12.8pp. US is pulling the overall number up.

ios.head: App Total Revenue +22.3% — up in line with the new subs signed up 7 days earlier (+76.8%).
ios.body: App Total Revenue on 10-29 vs 10-22 is +22.3%, and App Total New Subs on 10-22 vs 10-15 was +76.8% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (on 10-29 vs 10-22): Subscription +20.9%, Pay as you go +88.2%. This is the normal pattern, so no surprise is building up.

ios.head: App Total Revenue +14.0% — up mainly in Subscription (+1,565, +12.6%).
ios.body: App Total Revenue (YMK · US) was 14,469, against 12,693 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks (+1,776). By purchase type: Subscription +1,565 (+12.6%), Pay as you go +211 (+85.3%). Pay as you go is 3.2% of revenue. Subscription is the recurring part fed by new subs about a week earlier; look at new subs and renewals.

ios.head: App Total Install is moving faster than the other steps (+84.2% vs about +30.7%).
ios.body: App Total Install is +84.2% while the other steps are all moving about +30.7% — a gap of +53.5pp. When one step moves very differently from the rest, the cause is usually specific to that step.

insights.title: Revenue by purchase type — Subscription revenue is down 3.8%; Pay as you go +21.7% is softening it (total -2.3%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue was 75,359, against 77,147 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks (-1,788). By purchase type: Subscription -2,754 (-3.8%), Pay as you go +966 (+21.7%). Pay as you go is 7.2% of revenue. The recurring part is what new subs feed, so the Pay as you go lift is one-off cover, not a recovery.

insights.title: Purchase type by app — Subscription revenue is falling most in YCP (-9.4%), while YMK grows (+0.6%).
insights.body: By app: the biggest Subscription fall is YCP -2,708 (-9.4%, about 36% of revenue); Pay as you go moved most in YCV +721 (+55.6%); YCV relies most on Pay as you go (21% of its revenue vs 7.2% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Which app — App Total New User -16.0% is mostly YCP — not every app.
insights.body: App Total New User moved -16.0% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App -16.0%, YMK +7.5%, YCP -91.8%, YCV +5.9%). YCP accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Market trend — US is losing ground fast on turning installs into subs (-36.8%, now 11.0%).
insights.body: In US, 11.0% of installs now turn into new subs — -36.8% versus last period. It is about 40% of revenue (a big revenue market): fewer of the people downloading are subscribing, and revenue will feel that within a week or two.

insights.title: Install source — App Total Install -6.6% — Paid Install is behind most of it (-1,510, -12.8%).
insights.body: App Total Install was 25,459, against 27,265 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of -1,806. Where that came from: Paid Install -1,510 (-12.8%), SEO Install -939 (-39.2%), Organic Install +735 (+5.9%). Paid Install moved the most on its own (-1,510, -12.8%) and is now 40.4% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first. Going the other way at the same time: Organic Install +735.

insights.title: Install mix — Where installs come from is shifting away from SEO Install (-39.2% vs -6.6% for installs overall).
insights.body: SEO Install was 1,458, -39.2% against the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks, while total installs moved -6.6% — a difference of -32.6 percentage points. SEO Install is now 5.7% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving away from it; free traffic slipping while paid holds up means we are buying more of the same installs..

insights.title: Purchase type by country — Subscription revenue is falling most in MX (-30.8%), while CA grows (+50.0%).
insights.body: By country: the biggest Subscription fall is MX -892 (-30.8%, about 3% of revenue); the biggest Subscription gain is CA +760 (+50.0%); Pay as you go moved most in US +470 (+26.0%); JP relies most on Pay as you go (23% of its revenue vs 7.2% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Next period outlook — Expect App Total Revenue to recover in about 7 days — more of the people installing are subscribing, mostly YMK.
insights.body: App Total New Subs is +11.6% while App Total Install is only -6.6% — a bigger share of people who installed are subscribing than usual (+18.3pp more growth). New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So expect App Total Revenue to go up in about 7 days. App Total Revenue is -2.3% right now, so this points to a recovery rather than more weakness. Most of the increase comes from YMK (+22.8%); YCP is -14.1%.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue +11.3% — up in line with the new subs signed up 7 days earlier (+23.7%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue on 10-29 vs 10-22 is +11.3%, and App Total New Subs on 10-22 vs 10-15 was +23.7% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (on 10-29 vs 10-22): Subscription +10.1%, Pay as you go +29.7%. This is the normal pattern, so no surprise is building up.
